Hi,

I have quasi-solved the memory issue by reducing the number of points by a factor of 100 and changed Linux (64 bit) with 4GB RAM.

However, I am stuck with the contour colouring.  The z data is non-linear, but I can manually fix this in the data.  However, I would like to know how to create a custom colour for each bin, given I have 9 bins.  First bin is white, then green, then yellow....

Thanks,
Simon


On Thursday, 26 July 2012 23:03:14 UTC+2, psiphi75 wrote:
Hi,

I would like to reproduce the Global Seismic Hazard Map, at least in terms of colouring:
http://www.seismo.ethz.ch/static/GSHAP/ 

It does not need to be exact in terms of colouring, but it would be good to be similar to the eye.  At the moment I don't care about the rest of the map details like projection, land area, showing country borders, etc.  Disclaimer: I'm very new to R, but don't mind learning to get this done.

Where I am so far:
The problem is that the data set is large, more than 5 million points for the whole world.  I don't care about render time, but I am limited to memory which it seems to fail at the moment (see message below), so I have reduced my set to just Europe, in the end I need the globe.  I have used "stat_contour" to do this for now.  But since the data set is so large it would be good to reduce the data set somehow.

My Basic Code:

# load the data
dat = read.delim("GSHPUB.txt")

# Bound data to Europe only
lng_min = -20
lng_max = 30
lat_min = 30
lat_max = 70
dat <- dat[(lat_min < dat$Latitude & dat$Latitude < lat_max) & (lng_min < dat$Longitude & dat$Longitude < lng_max),]

# Plot a contour map
p <- ggplot(dat, aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude, z = PGA)) 
p + stat_contour(geom="polygon", na.rm=TRUE) + scale_colour_gradient(limits=c(0, 3), low = "green", high = "red")

Where I want to go from here:
How to plot the world data map, but get the following message: "Reached total allocation of 1535Mb: see help(memory.size)".   I currently use Win XP with 4GB of RAM, would I be better to try Linux?   How do I reduce the data set, but still keep it visually similar.
    How to change the gradient of the contour to the same as (or very similar to) the Global Seismic Hazard Map?

      Note: The raw data is available here: http://www.seismo.ethz.ch/static/gshap/global/caution.html

      Thanks
